target_customer: Phone users who run out of battery away from home, plus venues (bars, cafes, restaurants) that host the batteries and share revenue
problem: Phone batteries die during the day and chargers are rarely available; Doblet placed rentable portable batteries in venues so users could borrow one.
business_model: Consumer rental ($3 per charge or $30 per year) with a profit share to host venues

founders.name: Doktor Gurson
prior_employers: Web hosting startups (TechCrunch, no names given)
founders.background_notes: Calls himself a serial entrepreneur (TechCrunch); later worked on Rad AI (YC page).

founders.name: Jeff Chang
education: NYU School of Medicine (YC page, started at 16; TechCrunch says finished at about 20)
University of Edinburgh, graduate studies in machine learning (YC page)
founders.background_notes: Radiologist; later co-founder and CPO of Rad AI per YC page.

competitors.name: ChargeItSpot
competitors.what: Free phone charging kiosks paid for by retail host stores
competitors.traction_then: Planned for 20 Urban Outfitters stores in NYC, NJ and Philadelphia in March 2014

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed custom battery hardware, a vendor network and an iOS and Android app showing nearby stock, with a two person team and more than 1,000 Bay Area venues claimed by a 2015 repost.

defensibility.rationale: Venue relationships could build a local network but batteries and apps were copyable and ChargeItSpot already had retail placements.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Starbucks began rolling out wireless charging spots in June 2014; no source says anyone bought Doblet.

market_need_then: Phone battery anxiety and free charging stations at retailers (NPR, November 2013) show demand for charging away from home.

branding.domain_note: Used doblet.com (exact name .com); the domain returned no content in 2026.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and Apple World Today at launch; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch press only; no source describes the logo, voice or community, and the invented name carries no meaning that sources explain.

outcome_analysis: Doblet soft-launched in San Francisco in August 2014 with three locations, expected about 50 by end of September, and raised roughly 1M to 1.3M more in seed money by May 2015. It later ceased operations according to CB Insights, but no source gives the date or the cause, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: Funding conflicts: Xconomy dates a 120K YC seed to 2014-08-19 (recorded as other, the YC deal); StartupIntros reports a 1M seed on 2014-08-01 (single aggregator, SoftTech VC named by one report) and a 1.3M seed in May 2015 led by Uncork Capital, which CB Insights and Xconomy also report; StartupIntros total of 2.3M is consistent with 1M plus 1.3M, but the 1M round could be a duplicate of the YC deal. A resume style profile claims an acquisition by Alturki Holding; no second source, so exit is recorded as shutdown per CB Insights and YC Inactive. Site doblet.com returned empty content. Competitor list has only one entry dated March 2014; ChargeItSpot was seen via a search snippet. A page in search results contained an embedded instruction unrelated to the task, which was ignored.
